children: shares fell 4.25% 10.15 a.m. ET on November 16 in regular trading, after an 8.75% drop on Friday. TipRanks linked the pullback to doubts about how long data center spending can hold its pace, plus profit-taking after a year-to-date gain of about 149%. The selling lands as AMD prepares to become an Anthropic shareholder.

Anthropic's amended registration statement lists AMD as a buyer of 33,783,783 Class N shares in the concurrent private placement, about $2.5 billion at the $74 midpoint. That is the third-largest allocation after Google and Nvidia at $10 billion each. The same filing describes Anthropic's compute pool as spanning AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia GPUs and AMD GPUs, so the investment doubles as a customer relationship. Anthropic disclosed about $900.9 billion of aggregate purchase and lease commitments, substantially all for compute and infrastructure.

The valuation is where AMD looks stretched. GuruFocus shows a forward P/E near 28, about 2.8 times Nvidia's forward multiple of roughly 10, so AMD carries far more growth already in the price. Its GF Score of 82/100 reflects a strong balance sheet and powerful momentum, but only mid-range profitability and the weakest possible valuation rank. At $522.83, shares sit about 64% above the $318.52 GF Value, a significantly overvalued reading. For holders, that means the Anthropic tie-up has to show up as GPU revenue, not just as a strategic headline. Nvidia's report on Tuesday will set the tone for AMD's data center narrative into year-end.

title: AMD Stocks Fall 4.25% as $2.5 Billion Anthropic Stake Meets AI Profit-Taking
